Executive proposition

EMYRGEN proposes a Saudi Climate Intelligence capability that converts environmental data into operational action.

Identify and prioritize conditions affecting water efficiency, vegetation establishment, and land stability.
Deploy the right aircraft class for precision sensing, regional intelligence, or heavy unmanned logistics.
Provide one command-level operational picture across missions, sites, and outcomes.
Build a phased path from pilot program to enduring Saudi capability.
01 / National priorities

Environmental intelligence aligned to Saudi execution.

This proposal positions EMYRGEN as an operational partner supporting national environmental goals through persistent sensing, mission aviation, and outcome-focused field operations.

Water security

Improve irrigation prioritization, monitor stress signals earlier, and direct field teams toward the highest-value interventions.

Green Arabia

Protect large-scale restoration investments by screening vegetation corridors, soil conditions, and survival risk before losses spread.

Sand & dust resilience

Detect dust-source conditions, strengthen warning readiness, and support targeted mitigation in high-risk zones.

Remote logistics

Add unmanned heavy-lift capability for resupply, equipment delivery, and difficult-access operations across remote regions.

02 / Platform

Three aircraft classes. One mission architecture.

The strategic differentiator is not one aircraft alone, but the way three complementary aviation classes feed one Saudi operational picture—from precision local inspection to regional intelligence and heavy unmanned logistics.

EGX-10

Light autonomous VTOL for close-range inspection, precision sensing, and site-level environmental verification.

03 / Green Arabia

Protect every corridor, plantation, and water-fed restoration zone.

Saudi restoration programs deserve continuous operational visibility. EMYRGEN can help detect stress earlier, prioritize follow-up action faster, and verify whether interventions are improving outcomes on the ground.

Water & irrigation insight

Screen broad planted areas to identify irregularity, underperformance, and developing stress that deserves inspection.

Vegetation survival monitoring

Track establishment conditions and compare areas over time so resources go where they can protect the most value.

Operational prioritization

Turn environmental observations into site-level tasking for teams, equipment, and follow-up verification flights.

04 / Mission concept

Operation Green Arabia.
From observation to measured outcome.

The mission architecture links upstream awareness with field action. The result is a practical operating cycle that Saudi stakeholders can pilot, evaluate, and scale.

01

Observe

Integrate satellite, site, and aviation-derived environmental signals.

02

Prioritize

Identify sites where water stress, vegetation risk, or dust conditions justify operational attention.

03

Task aircraft

Deploy EGX-10, EGX-200, or converted unmanned helicopter based on mission need.

04

Verify

Capture local observations, aerial sensing, or payload delivery results at the site level.

05

Act

Support field operations, follow-up inspections, and logistical movement to the right location.

06

Measure

Compare outcomes across time and sites to inform next decisions and scale-up strategy.

05 / Aircraft conversion & readiness

Heavy unmanned capability built through helicopter conversion.

The heavy class is not a generic graphic. It represents a serious pathway: converting suitable helicopters into unmanned systems that can extend Saudi reach in remote operations.

Payload movement

Transport equipment, sensors, field supplies, or mission packages to difficult-access locations.

Engineering confidence

Pair flight-platform conversion with avionics integration, remote operations, and maintenance discipline.

Saudi localization potential

Build a program structure that can support local technical capability, operations, and long-term sustainment.

06 / Sand & dust intelligence

Turn atmospheric awareness into protective action.

Saudi Arabia already invests in sand-and-dust monitoring. EMYRGEN can add an operational aviation layer that strengthens environmental observation, hotspot assessment, and infrastructure readiness.

Dust-source monitoring

Survey priority areas and build better understanding of conditions associated with source activation and movement.

Infrastructure protection

Support earlier preparation for airports, roads, industrial facilities, energy sites, and high-value public assets.

Integrated resilience

Link dust intelligence with vegetation, soil, water, and restoration strategies instead of treating the problem in isolation.

08 / National impact

A phased path from pilot to enduring Saudi capability.

The right first step is a focused pilot: prove operational value, refine the mission model, and establish the foundation for long-term Saudi deployment and localization.

Phase 1

Scoping

Select the use cases, pilot geography, partner entities, operational KPIs, and deployment model.

Phase 2

Pilot execution

Deploy the initial sensing and mission architecture for water, greening, dust, and field logistics scenarios.

Phase 3

Validation

Measure decision value, field efficiency, response speed, and environmental outcome indicators.

Phase 4

Scale-up

Extend toward a durable Saudi operational capability with localized teams, assets, and governance.

Strategic partnership proposal

Position EMYRGEN as a Saudi partner for environmental intelligence and autonomous field operations.

The immediate objective is to align on a pilot program: define the lead use case, confirm the operating stakeholders, and structure a practical demonstration path that can mature into national capability.
